headline: Fleet discipline lifts profit despite softer rental demand
summary_short: Avis Budget's Q2 2026 revenue fell 1% y/y to $2,998M as rental demand softened, but net income rose to $35M from $4M and Adjusted EBITDA grew 3% y/y to $286M on record vehicle utilization (72.6%, +1.9pts y/y) and 4% lower per-unit fleet costs.
summary_long: Revenue fell 1% y/y to $2,998M (Americas -2%, International flat) as rental days dropped 2% while pricing held flat — softer volume, not price, drove the dip. Net income rose to $35M from $4M y/y as pretax income improved to $73M from $15M, helped by an 8% drop in vehicle depreciation ($583M vs $636M) and lower restructuring charges ($18M vs $59M). Adjusted EBITDA grew 3% y/y to $286M (Americas +8% to $237M, International -11% to $73M) as the company resized its fleet, lifting utilization to a Q2-record 72.6% and cutting per-unit fleet costs 4% to $290/month. Liquidity was ~$1.0B plus $1.9B of fleet funding capacity.

drivers.explanation: Americas revenue -2% y/y matches a 2% drop in rental days (32.6M vs 33.3M) against flat-to-slightly-higher pricing ($70.20 vs $70.03 RPD); softer transaction volume, not price, drove the y/y decline.
Pretax income rose to $73M from $15M as vehicle depreciation fell 8% y/y ($583M vs $636M) and restructuring charges fell to $18M from $59M, outweighing roughly flat operating and SG&A costs.
EPS rose from $0.10 to $0.98 y/y roughly in step with net income's swing, since diluted share count was nearly flat (35.7M vs 35.4M).

This shard field is a naive EBITDA that adds back vehicle depreciation ($583M) and vehicle interest ($232M); Avis's own Adjusted EBITDA ($286M) treats those as core operating costs, explaining the large gap between the two measures.

CEO Choi said the company resized its fleet quickly as booking trends softened, lifting Total Company vehicle utilization to a Q2-record 72.6% (+1.9pts y/y) and cutting per-unit fleet costs 4% to $290/month, delivering Adjusted EBITDA in line with initial expectations.
